title: Wrapper can dispatch a second live CLI session against one claim
description:
Filed by governor-1a5aca5d 12:56Z under the human's standing sweep directive, from THREE measured occurrences in one session (2026-08-16):

THE DEFECT. The agent wrapper can start a second CLI session for a workerId whose previous session is still alive and holding a claim. Both sessions then execute the same task concurrently in the shared worktree. The registry cannot see the duplicate — moe.list_workers shows ONE worker on the task because both sessions share the workerId; presence/staleness is per-workerId, not per-session.

OCCURRENCES, all disclosed in #general/#governors:
1. task-48c0c0db ~12:29Z: two live sessions under worker-5678886b; the earlier stood down mid-race (msg-ebbb27c0), the later committed. Resolved by luck + discipline: the earlier session happened to notice the other's drill cycling via file hashes.
2. task-6cbff010 ~12:55Z: same workerId, second session resumed at step-2 while the first had already LANDED the task into REVIEW (msg-7061495940) — the second session was working a stale plan state against moved bytes.
3. (Earlier class, 00:16: the wrapper re-dispatched task-b785 to a fresh worker while the prior worker's claim state was ambiguous — logged as wrapper-can-dispatch-an-already-claimed-task.)

BLAST RADIUS: duplicate mutation drills in the shared worktree, racing commits into one index, double complete_step calls, and QA grading a moving target. Only worker discipline (collision notes, stand-downs) prevented corruption each time.

LIKELY SEAM: the wrapper's crash-resume path ("CLI session ended N times... pausing auto-resume") plus its fresh-dispatch path can both fire after an outage window; nothing fences session generation. Fix directions the planner should weigh (measure first): a per-session nonce/generation in the registry so heartbeat/claims from a superseded session are refused with a stable code; wrapper-side single-flight lock per workerId; or daemon-side rejection of a second concurrent session registration for a live workerId.

Verification: a test that simulates two sessions under one workerId proves the second is refused (or fenced) with a stable reason code, and the first's claim/heartbeat continues unaffected.
definitionOfDone: The double-dispatch seam is identified by measurement (wrapper resume path and/or daemon registration) and the chosen fencing mechanism is implemented so a second concurrent session for a live workerId is refused or superseded with a stable reason code — never silently co-active.
The superseded/refused session's tool calls (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send) fail closed with that code rather than mutating task state.
A test simulates the two-session race and pins the refusal code and layer; a mutation drill removing the fence turns it red.
The three occurrence records above are cited in the completion note as the reproduced-class evidence.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; a fenced-out session must not be able to corrupt the claim, the worktree index, or the step ledger.
Do not break single-session resume-after-crash — the fence distinguishes a NEW session superseding a dead one (allowed, current behavior) from a second session co-existing with a LIVE one (refused).
Re-measure the wrapper dispatch/resume code paths on current bytes before planning; the occurrence timeline above is evidence, not a code map.

implementationPlan.description: SCOPE AND SEAM, by measurement, before any edit. Read-only step. The occurrence list in the description is from the OLD Moe harness (its tool names are moe.list_workers / heartbeat / complete_step). Epic rail 2 pins all development to D:/projexts/moe-next, so this task fixes the SAME DEFECT CLASS in moe-next's own wrapper and claim surfaces, and the completion note must say plainly that the old-Moe harness instance is out of scope under that rail. Re-confirm the architect's measurement at committed HEAD with `git grep`, do not trust this text: (a) moe-next ALREADY fences most of the class -- `work.claim` refuses a held item with the stable code `WORK_CLAIM_HELD` at layer `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` (apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts:160) and a non-claimant with `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT` (:176), the frozen list being work/work-claim-contracts.ts:47-53; session generations already exist and a superseded generation refuses (apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts:206 at layer BINDING, :355 SESSION_REPLAYED at layer GENERATION). (b) The wrapper serialises passes (`runOnce`, agent-wrapper.ts:355-365), skips items whose durable surface shows `step.claim !== null`, and holds an `active` Map keyed by workItemId (:343). THE HOLE: that `active` Map is IN-PROCESS ONLY, and the durable claim carries `expiresAt = clock() + claimTtlMs` (30 minutes, set in agent-wrapper-main.ts). When a claim EXPIRES while its agent child is still alive -- or when the wrapper process restarts with an empty `active` Map -- the surface reports the item unclaimed again and a SECOND live agent is staffed on it. The first child is never told; it keeps writing files in the shared worktree and only learns of the loss when a later command returns WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT. Write the confirmed seam into the step note naming exact files and lines. If measurement shows the hole is already closed, STOP and report that rather than adding a second fence.

(a) EXISTING FENCES — verified present, so they are COMPOSED, not rebuilt:
- work-claim-services.ts:160 `refuse(request.kind, "WORK_CLAIM_HELD", "DAEMON_PREREQUISITE")`; :176 `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT`, same layer. Frozen list work-claim-contracts.ts:49/:51.
- session-authority.ts:355 `if (rotation === null) return refuse("SESSION_REPLAYED", "GENERATION")`; BINDING refusals at :62/:64.

(b) THE HOLE — traced end to end, and it is worse than "the Map is in-process":
1. work-claim-services.ts:134 `return record.expiresAt > decidedAt ? record : null` — `activeClaim` returns NULL once a claim is past expiry.
2. affordance-read.ts:74-76 `claimFields` calls `activeClaim(record, now)` and emits `claim: active === null ? null : {...}`. So an EXPIRED claim projects onto the surface as `claim: null` — indistinguishable from never-claimed.
3. agent-wrapper.ts:339 `if (step.status !== "READY" || step.claim !== null) continue` therefore STOPS skipping the item.
4. agent-wrapper.ts:343 `if (active.has(workItemIdFor(...))) continue` is then the ONLY remaining guard, and `active` is a process-local Map (set :314, deleted :313 in `.finally`). A wrapper restart empties it; a second wrapper process never had it.
5. Claim TTL is 30 minutes (agent-wrapper-main.ts:199 `claimTtlMs: 30 * 60 * 1000`). An agent child alive past 30 minutes — routine for a coding session — outlives its own claim.

DECISIVE DETAIL the plan predicted and I confirmed: `claimFields` sets `claimAggregateVersion: record?.version ?? 0` REGARDLESS of expiry (affordance-read.ts:81). So the second staffing pass carries the correct expectedVersion into `work.claim` (agent-wrapper.ts:248-249) and the command layer COMMITS it — `activeClaim` already returned null at :156, so WORK_CLAIM_HELD never fires. Nothing at any layer refuses the second live session. The first child is not told; it learns only when a later command returns WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT. This is exactly the reported class, and it confirms the architect's rejected-option (e): reusing WORK_CLAIM_HELD for the expired-but-live case would be a false statement about what the durable claim says.

(c) NOT ALREADY CLOSED — the plan's stop condition does not fire. `git grep -rln "liveChild|live_child|spawnRecord|staffing|agent-session-fence|sessionFence" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src packages/` returns only agent-wrapper-main.ts, agent-wrapper.test.ts and wrapper-knobs.test.ts, all prose/test matches; no durable live-child record module exists. `git ls-tree HEAD apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/` confirms no agent-session-fence.* file.

SIZE NOTE carried into step 4: agent-wrapper.ts is ALREADY 375 physical lines at HEAD — above the 250 target and 25 below the 400 split threshold, a pre-existing condition I did not create. I will keep the step-4 composition to a small call site and, if it approaches 400, extract the staffing gate into a sibling module as step 4 directs, never by trimming a refusal branch.

implementationPlan.description: RED on the fence contract, in a new apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.test.ts over a REAL SqliteEventStore opened on a temp file. The fence answers one question: may this wrapper staff this work item right now? Failing tests first: (1) item with no durable claim and no recorded live child -> ADMIT; (2) item with an ACTIVE unexpired claim -> refuse with the exact stable code and layer (assert both literals, never `ok === false`); (3) item whose claim has EXPIRED but whose durable live-child record has not been retired -> refuse with a DISTINCT stable code -- this is the reported class and it must not collapse into the held-claim code, or a later guard change makes the test vacuous; (4) item whose claim expired AND whose child was durably recorded as terminated -> ADMIT, because a genuinely dead predecessor must still be replaceable (task rail 2: single-session resume-after-crash must keep working); (5) a second fence query for the same item while the first admission is unretired, asked through a REOPENED store handle -> still refuses with the case-3 code, proving the record is durable rather than in-process. Every refusal asserts code AND layer, and every refusal case asserts the store's raw event count did not change.
implementationPlan.note:
RED landed: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.test.ts, 6 cases over a REAL file-backed SqliteEventStore (SqliteEventStore.openForProject on an mkdtempSync temp dir), not an ephemeral one — case 5 reopens the same .db path and an in-memory store could not express that.

Run: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.test.ts`
Result: `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Error: Cannot find module './agent-session-fence.js'`. RED for the intended reason — the module does not exist yet. (Focused daemon runs need `--root . --config package.json`; without them vitest resolves the ROOT config, whose include never covers apps/** and reports "No test files found".)

CASES, mapped to the plan:
1. no durable claim + no live child -> ADMIT.
2. ACTIVE unexpired claim -> refuse `AGENT_STAFFING_CLAIM_HELD` at layer AGENT_STAFFING_LAYER.
3. EXPIRED claim + unretired live child -> refuse `AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE` — the reported class, on a DISTINCT code.
4. expired claim + child durably retired -> ADMIT (task rail 2: a dead predecessor must stay replaceable, or the fence becomes a permanent wedge).
5. second query through a REOPENED store handle -> still `AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE`, which is what separates a durable record from the in-process Map that already exists.
Plus a vocabulary case pinning that the two causes never collapse onto one code.

Every refusal asserts BOTH the literal code and the layer (never `ok === false`), and every refusal case asserts `store.readEventHorizon()` is unchanged across the call — a gate that refuses but writes has mutated durable state on an inert path.

WHY CASE 3 CANNOT GO VACUOUS: at `AFTER_EXPIRY` the durable claim is already expired, so `activeClaim` returns null and the claim branch cannot answer. Only the live-child record can produce that refusal. If case 3 ever reports the held-claim code, the suite is telling me the causes collapsed.

FIXTURE HONESTY: claims are seeded through the production `runWorkClaimCommand`, never by writing a store row by hand — a hand-built row could encode a claim shape no real command can produce, and the fence would be proven against a fiction.

CONTRACT THE FENCE MUST IMPLEMENT (step 3): `createAgentSessionFence({ projectId, store })` returning `admit(workItemId, now)`, `recordLiveChild({ claimAggregateVersion, sessionId, workItemId })`, `retireLiveChild(workItemId)`; plus exported `AGENT_STAFFING_LAYER` and the frozen `AGENT_STAFFING_REFUSAL_CODES`.

HANDLE HYGIENE: every opened handle is closed in `afterEach` (including the pre-reopen handle, popped from the tracking array after its explicit close so it is not double-closed) and temp roots are removed with `rmSync(..., { maxRetries: 5 })`. A held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker outright.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the fence. Create apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./agent-session-fence.ts";` -- without it the module is invisible to the .js import graph). Export a durable admission port: record that a work item has a live spawned child (session id, work item id, the claim aggregate version admitted against), query whether staffing is admissible, and retire the record when the child exits. Declare the fence's stable refusal codes as a frozen exported constant list in this module so tests assert a named constant rather than a bare string; do NOT widen `WORK_CLAIM_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES` -- that list belongs to the work-claim command surface and this is a wrapper-side staffing decision, so a new member there would be a false claim about which layer refuses. Fail closed on every unreadable, throwing, or ambiguous durable read: it refuses staffing, it never admits. Keep the file <=250 physical lines and perform no spawning here -- this module decides, the wrapper acts.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. Created apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.ts (199 physical lines, within the 250 target) plus its one-line `.js` bridge `export * from "./agent-session-fence.ts";` matching the sibling convention in agent-authority-cleanup.js.

Run: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/agent-session-fence.test.ts`
Result: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 6 passed (6)` — a real count line, not an exit-0 vacuum.

SHAPE. `createAgentSessionFence({ projectId, store })` exposes `admit(workItemId, now)`, `recordLiveChild(record)`, `retireLiveChild(workItemId)`. Exported `AGENT_STAFFING_LAYER = "WRAPPER_STAFFING"` and the frozen `AGENT_STAFFING_REFUSAL_CODES` = CLAIM_HELD / CHILD_LIVE / RECORD_UNREADABLE. These are deliberately NOT added to WORK_CLAIM_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES: that list belongs to the work-claim command surface, and a member there would misname which layer refused a wrapper-side staffing decision. No spawning happens in this module — it decides, the wrapper acts.

DURABILITY. The record is an append-only pair of events (`AgentStaffingAdmitted` / `AgentStaffingRetired`) on a dedicated aggregate `wrapper-staffing/<sha256(workItemId)>`, committed through `store.commit`. The id is hashed because a work item id is caller-shaped and must not decide an aggregate id's length or charset. The fold sorts by `aggregateSequence` and lets the last transition win, so ADMITTED with no later RETIRED means a child is still live — which is what survives the wrapper restart that the in-process Map cannot.

FAIL CLOSED, three ways, all refusing rather than admitting: a throwing `readWorkClaimLedger` or `readEvents`; the claim ledger's own `unreadable` flag (a corrupt ledger must never read as "nobody holds it"); and an UNKNOWN event type on the staffing aggregate, which is treated as UNREADABLE rather than skipped — a skipped event is exactly how a fold silently starts admitting. `admit` performs no writes, which the tests pin by asserting `readEventHorizon()` is unchanged across every refusal.

ORDER OF THE TWO GATES: the claim is consulted first, then the live child. At an expired claim the first gate cannot answer (activeClaim returns null), so only the live-child record can produce CHILD_LIVE — that is what keeps test case 3 from going vacuous.

implementationPlan.note:
Fence composed into the wrapper. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/` -> `Test Files 9 passed (9)`, `Tests 91 passed (91)`. No pre-existing wrapper case changed behaviour.

COMPOSITION, exactly where the step directed:
- `staffingFence` added to `AgentWrapperConfig` as an injected port; the wrapper never constructs a store handle.
- Consulted in `staff` BEFORE `session.open` and BEFORE `work.claim`. One consult fences both because both follow that point. On refusal it returns the fence's own code as the SpawnReport outcome, so the layer that answered stays visible.
- The in-process `active.has(...)` guard is UNTOUCHED and still runs. The gate is added, not substituted — a comment at the `gate` construction says so, because a later reader deleting "the redundant check" is the obvious way this regresses.
- `recordLiveChild` fires immediately after admission, BEFORE the lifetime handlers attach; a record written later could be skipped by a child that exits instantly.
- `retireLiveChild` is called on BOTH exit routes — explicitly in the fulfilment callback and again in the rejection callback, not once in `.finally`. Two separate call sites is deliberate: drill 3 removes the rejection-side one, and a single `.finally` would leave that drill nothing to delete.

implementationPlan.description: THE RACE TEST plus the superseded-side proof, both in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts (extend it; no parallel suite). RACE (DoD 4): drive two `runOnce` passes against one surface where the first pass has spawned and the claim has been aged past `expiresAt` via the injected `clock`; assert the second pass emits a SpawnReport whose outcome is the exact fence code from step 3, and that `config.spawnAgent` was called exactly ONCE -- assert the call COUNT, because a second spawn that later failed would otherwise pass. SUPERSEDED SIDE (DoD 3): the DoD names old-Moe tools (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send); map them in the step note to moe-next's real equivalents and test those -- after a second session is admitted for an item, the FIRST session's `work.renew` must refuse with the literal `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT` at layer `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, and a command carrying the superseded session generation must refuse through the existing session-authority path with its literal code and layer. Assert WHICH layer refused in each case: two layers can answer here, and a test asserting only "refused" is one added guard away from vacuous. Finally assert the refused commands mutated nothing by re-reading the work aggregate and comparing canonical bytes before and after.
implementationPlan.note:
Three cases added to apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts (extended, no parallel suite). `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 29 passed (29)`. Confirmed by NAME under --reporter=verbose that all three new cases actually executed, rather than trusting the count to have grown:
  ✓ ... durable staffing fence > refuses a second wrapper's pass while the first child is live, and spawns ONCE (28ms)
  ✓ ... durable staffing fence > refuses the SUPERSEDED session's work.renew at the work-claim layer, mutating nothing (23ms)
  ✓ ... durable staffing fence > refuses an unopened session credential at the identity layer (12ms)

THE RACE. Pass 1 spawns and records a live child. Pass 2 comes from a SECOND `createAgentWrapper` instance whose fence sits on a REOPENED store handle — a restarted wrapper with an empty `active` map. That shape is the point: a same-instance second pass is refused by the in-process map at :343 and would prove nothing about durability, which is exactly the trap drill 1 exists to catch. Asserted: pass 2's SpawnReport outcome is the literal `AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE` with `sessionId: null` (nothing was minted), and `spawnCalls` is still `[target]` — the COUNT, because a second spawn that failed afterwards would still have put two live children in the shared worktree, which IS the defect.

Two things the race test asserts rather than assumes:
- The surface is narrowed to ONE staffable item, so "spawned exactly once" is exact instead of "once for this item plus whatever else the board offered". Without it the wrapper legitimately moves on to the next unclaimed step after a refusal (active.size does not grow on a refusal) and the count assertion would be measuring the board's shape, not the fence.
- The defect's precondition is asserted directly: after the child is live the surface step reads `{ claim: null, status: "READY" }`. If that ever stops holding, the test is no longer reproducing the reported class and should fail loudly rather than pass for a new reason.

WHY THE EXPIRY IS INJECTED, NOT SLEPT. The affordance surface judges claim expiry against the PROVIDER's real clock, not the wrapper's injected one, so aging `config.clock` cannot age the surface. Reaching a genuinely expired projection would mean either a real 60s sleep or a ~1ms TTL — and a 1ms TTL also expires the agent's SESSION, whose authentication is judged against the same real clock, so the first pass's own `work.claim` would fail and the test would be measuring a broken setup. The projection is instead injected in the port. It is not assumed anywhere: the `activeClaim` -> `claim: null` chain is measured on disk in step 1 and driven against a REAL expired claim over a real store in agent-session-fence.test.ts case 3.

DoD 2 MAPPED TO REAL TOOLS. The DoD names old-Moe tools (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send); none exist in moe-next. The real equivalents tested here: `work.renew` (the claim holder's keepalive and the first command a superseded session actually hits) and session credential authentication.
- Work-claim layer: a superseded principal's `work.renew` refuses with literal `code: "WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT"` and `refusedBy: "DAEMON_PREREQUISITE"`. Note the field is `refusedBy`, not `layer` — measured off the `refuse()` helper at work-claim-services.ts:56-65 rather than assumed from the plan's prose.
- Mutated nothing: the work aggregate is re-read and compared as canonical JSON bytes before/after the refusal, plus a field assertion that the claim still names `sess-second` at version 3.
- Identity layer: pinned in its own case, with the finding that this layer answers `{ verdict: "UNAUTHENTICATED" }` — a VERDICT carrying no reason code. Recorded explicitly because a reader assuming a coded refusal here would write an assertion that can never match. Paired with an AUTHENTICATED control on the operator credential so the case cannot be satisfied by an authenticator that refuses everything.

HONEST LIMIT, stated rather than dressed up: I did NOT produce a live `SESSION_REPLAYED`/`GENERATION` refusal. Reaching that branch needs a recovery-incarnation or key-epoch change (see genesis-first-boot.test.ts:230) and, per the known core-binding gotcha, a naive superseded-credential probe refuses at BINDING before `isCurrentGeneration` ever runs — so a test claiming to cover GENERATION would most likely be covering BINDING while looking correct. Both layers that DO answer on this path are pinned with their literal codes/verdicts instead.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, one per distinct claim, because "the fence exists" and "the fence fails closed" are different assertions. Drill 1 (the durable gate is load-bearing): delete the fence consultation from `staff`, leaving the in-process `active.has` check intact; the step-5 race test must go RED on its spawn-call-count assertion. If it stays green, the test is proving the in-process map rather than the durable fence -- reopen the fence's store between passes and re-run. Drill 2 (unreadable admits nothing): make the fence's unreadable-record branch return ADMIT instead of refusing; a named step-2 test must go RED. Drill 3 (the retire path is real): remove the retire call from the REJECTION branch of the `exit` handler; the case-4 dead-predecessor test must go RED, proving a crashed child does not permanently wedge the item. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME, and the exact assertion that failed -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the binding. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in this shared worktree), and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted per drilled file. One drill at a time: a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.
implementationPlan.note:
Three drills run ONE AT A TIME, each restored and hash-verified before the next. Post-drill: `sha256sum -c` on both drilled files -> both `OK`, byte-identical to the pre-drill baseline. Full suite after restore: `src/orchestrator/` -> `Test Files 9 passed (9)`, `Tests 96 passed (96)`.

Restores were done by RE-EDITING and verified by sha256, not by `git diff --numstat`. That matters here: agent-session-fence.ts is UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to it and would have reported a clean tree with a live mutation on disk. agent-wrapper.ts is tracked but already carries this task's step-4 diff, so its numstat is never 0/0 either. A content hash is the only restore proof that actually holds for both.

DRILL 1 — the durable gate is load-bearing. Deleted the fence consultation from `staff`, left the in-process `active.has` intact.
FIRST ATTEMPT REDDENED FOR THE WRONG REASON AND I DID NOT ACCEPT IT. It failed on the OUTCOME assertion with `WORK_CLAIM_HELD`, not on the count — meaning the existing work-claim layer was answering, and my race test was NOT reproducing the defect. Cause: the test faked `claim: null` in the port while the DURABLE claim was still unexpired, so `work.claim` refused on its own and the fence was never load-bearing. A green-after-restore here would have shipped a test that proves someone else's guard.
FIX: produce the defect state DURABLY instead of faking the projection — after the first pass spawns, the agent session's claim is RELEASED through the production `work.release` command. A released claim and an expired one are the same fact to every reader on this path (`activeClaim` returns null for both), and release is reachable deterministically where expiry would need a real 60s sleep or a TTL so short it also expires the agent's own session mid-handshake. The injected `claim: null` hack is gone; the surface now genuinely reports the item unclaimed.
I also moved the count assertion BEFORE the outcome assertion so the count is what reddens, as the step requires.

FAILING TEST: "createAgentWrapper — durable staffing fence > refuses a second wrapper's pass while the first child is live, and spawns ONCE"
FAILING ASSERTION (line 1234): `expect(spawnCalls).toEqual([target])` — received TWO entries, both `policy.install@proj-wrapper-fence-race-policy`. The same work item staffed twice with a live child on it: the reported defect, reproduced.

FAILING ASSERTION (agent-session-fence.test.ts:189): expected `{code: "AGENT_STAFFING_RECORD_UNREADABLE", layer: "WRAPPER_STAFFING", ok: false}`, received `{ok: true}`.
NOTE: this drill had NOTHING TO REDDEN when I started — none of my step-2 cases drove the unreadable branch. Rather than record a green drill, I added the missing case first: it commits a real event of an unknown type to the staffing aggregate through `store.commit` and requires the fold to refuse. Driving it with a real committed event rather than a stubbed reader is what makes it a test of production behaviour.

DRILL 3 — the retire path is real. Removed the retire call from the REJECTION branch of the `exit` handler ONLY, leaving the fulfilment branch intact.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the owned diff as an attacker: does the fence ever admit on an unreadable, throwing, or absent-but-ambiguous read? Can a restarted wrapper admit because the answer was in-process after all -- prove it by reopening the store in a test. Does the retire path run on EVERY exit route including the throw path and the containment-failure path, or can one route wedge an item forever? That would be a denial of service worse than the race, and the task rail's do-not-break-resume clause forbids it. Does the new refusal code collide with an existing one, and does each distinct cause keep a distinct code? Is `maxAgents` still honoured, and is the in-process `active` map still in place rather than replaced? Confirm no production file exceeds 250 physical lines. Cite the three occurrence records from the description (task-48c0c0db ~12:29Z, task-6cbff010 ~12:55Z, and the 00:16 re-dispatch class) in the completion note as DoD 5 requires, and state explicitly that the old-Moe harness instance of this defect is out of scope under epic rail 2. Then run `git status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry with `git restore --staged -- <path>`, and commit ONLY the five owned paths by explicit pathspec; verify with `git show --stat` that no foreign path appears. If a foreign whole-tree completion already captured these bytes, do NOT amend or reset -- record the merge-base diff for QA instead.

Verification gate. Read-only step. Run in the FOREGROUND, chained with `&&` so a red leg cannot be masked (a `;` chain reports only the last command; a pipe reports the tail's exit code): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck`. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code -- `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when the package name does not resolve, so a filtered leg is evidence only if it prints a `Test Files N passed` line with N nonzero; `@moe/daemon` resolves to apps/daemon. Confirm the new fence test file and the race test appear by name in the run output. Repo-wide red is compared to the merge-base baseline and may be disclosed only when the new failing-path delta intersected with this task's owned paths is empty; red inside the owned paths is a block, not a disclosure. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (a) fixing the old-Moe harness where the occurrences were observed -- epic rail 2 pins all development to D:/projexts/moe-next, so the deliverable is the same defect class closed in moe-next's own wrapper; the completion note must disclose that rather than let the title imply the harness was fixed. (b) A wrapper-side in-process lock -- one already exists (`active` Map plus serialised `runOnce`) and it is precisely what fails when the wrapper restarts or a second wrapper runs; more in-process state closes nothing. (c) Shortening claimTtlMs -- that shrinks the window but makes an expired-claim-over-a-live-child more frequent, not less. (d) Refusing all staffing on an expired claim -- breaks task rail 2, which requires resume-after-crash to keep working; the distinction the fence must draw is dead predecessor (admit) versus live predecessor whose claim merely expired (refuse). (e) Reusing WORK_CLAIM_HELD for the expired-but-live case, or adding the new codes to WORK_CLAIM_PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES -- collapsing causes makes the new test one guard away from vacuous, and putting a wrapper-side staffing decision in the command surface's frozen list would misname which layer refused. Chose a small durable admission record consulted by the wrapper before session.open and work.claim, retired on every child-exit route, with a distinct stable code per cause and its own exported frozen code list.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at committed HEAD a42ae2f with `git grep <sym> HEAD`; the working tree is foreign-dirty and must not be trusted. Most of this fence already exists and must be COMPOSED, not rebuilt. DURABLE CLAIM: apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts:160 refuses `WORK_CLAIM_HELD` and :176 refuses `WORK_CLAIM_NOT_CLAIMANT`, both at layer DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; the frozen list is work/work-claim-contracts.ts:47-53; the kinds are work.claim/work.release/work.renew (:18-22). SESSION GENERATIONS: apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority.ts mints generation 1 (:164, :168), rotates to generation+1 on renew (:341), refuses a mismatched held generation at :206 (layer BINDING) and refuses a replayed rotation at :355 with SESSION_REPLAYED (layer GENERATION) -- supersession semantics exist, so this task consumes them rather than adding a parallel notion. WRAPPER: createAgentWrapper at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:141; `staff` mints a FRESH sessionId per spawn (`sess-wrap-${mintSecret()}`, :206), opens the session under the operator credential (:231), then has the AGENT claim under its own credential so the durable fence names the agent (:248); passes are serialised by `runOnce` (:355-365); staffing skips `step.claim !== null` and `active.has(workItemId)` (:339-343); the child's `exit` handler retires `active` and runs cleanupAuthority on BOTH fulfilment and rejection (:301-314), which is the natural retire hook. THE HOLE: `active` is a process-local Map and the claim carries a 30-minute expiresAt set in agent-wrapper-main.ts, so an expired claim over a still-live child, or a wrapper restart, re-opens staffing for an item that already has a running agent. NOTE for the worker: DoD 3's tool names (heartbeat, complete_step, chat_send) are old-Moe tools; the moe-next equivalents to test are work.renew, the work-progress command, and session credential authentication.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a fence that is really the in-process map wearing a new name -- drill 1 exists to catch exactly that, and the race test must age the clock AND reopen the fence's backing store so the second pass cannot be refused by leftover memory. Second, a permanent wedge: if the retire path misses any exit route (throw, containment failure, process kill) an item becomes unstaffable forever, which is worse than the race it fixes and violates the task rail on resume-after-crash; drill 3 pins it. Third, two layers can refuse a superseded session (work-claim prerequisite and session-authority generation), so the DoD 3 tests must assert WHICH layer answered -- a second layer starting to answer first is the classic way these tests go quietly vacuous. Fourth, distinct causes need distinct codes; reusing WORK_CLAIM_HELD for the expired-but-live case would make case 3 indistinguishable from case 2. Fifth, close every SqliteEventStore handle on every path in tests -- a held handle kills the vitest worker outright. Sixth, mutation drills in this shared worktree must be restored by re-editing and verified with `git diff --numstat`; `git checkout` destroys peers' uncommitted work, and a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch so git reads clean. Finally, do not remove the existing in-process guard: it is still the correct cheap check inside one process, and the plan adds a gate rather than replacing one.
